newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf states advised to improve investment climate.
newsitem.headline: Gulf states advised to improve investment climate.

text.p: Gulf states must develop a strategy to attract foreign direct investment (FDI) to help diversify their oil-based economies, the Gulf Organisation for Industrial Consulting (GOIC) said.

GOIC -- which advises governments of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on economic policy -- said in a report they needed to improve their investment climate to attract FDI flows and encourage the repatriation of some $200 billion in Gulf capital invested in the United States and Europe.
"The GCC authorities must...develop a well-defined strategy and identify the foreign investing companies whose strategies are in harmony with their own," Doha-based GOIC said.
It said the Gulf states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar -- received only $1.2 billion of over $300 billion in FDI flows in 1995.

"There is an increasing competition among countries for a greater share of FDI. The countries which can offer secure and sound investment opportunities are likely to be the largest recipients," it said.
"By improving their investment climate, the GCC states can attract more FDI and encourage the repatriation of the GCC capital invested in the U.S. and Europe, amounting to about $200 billion."
GOIC was set up and is funded by the GCC.
